title: chore(deps): resolve @objectstack/* 17.5.0, and the zod 4.6.5 it requires, in pnpm-lock.yaml (objectui#11073)
body:
Fixes #11073

Clause-②: no — consumes the already-published `@objectstack` 17.5.0 contract by version; objectui adds no key, export or flag of its own, and every accept-set movement arriving through spec-by-reference pairs is enumerated in the PR for review

## What this PR is, at this head

`pnpm-lock.yaml` now resolves `@objectstack/*` 17.5.0 (was 17.4.0), plus the `zod` 4.6.5 that 17.5.0 requires. No manifest range moves in this PR and no objectui package `version` moves. The PM asked for the draft to open at the first compilable step, so this body records the readings taken on the lockfile-only head. Commits that adapt objectui to the published contract follow on this branch. The final gate readings, commit by commit, go into the `os-dev-report` comment on objectui#11073. Any later change to this body is for the seat to write.

It is expected to be RED on this head, for measured reasons (below). ⛔ No red here is waved through or re-run.

## H1 — premise (measured)

- Base `origin/main` `c80236e`: the lock resolved `@objectstack/{spec,types,sdui-parser,lint,formula,core,client}` at 17.4.0, and npm `latest` for all seven is 17.5.0.
- Manifests declare caret ranges only: `@objectstack/spec` at `^17.0.0` in 23 places, `^17.4.0` in 6, `^17.1.0` in 2 and `^17.3.0` in 1; `@objectstack/client` at `^17.3.0` in 2; `formula` and `lint` at `^17.0.0` in 2 each.
- objectui's `pnpm.overrides` (root `package.json`) and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` hold no `@objectstack` entry.
- ⇒ every range already admits 17.5.0, so a within-range regeneration moves the resolution without touching a range.

## H2 — how the lock was regenerated, and everything that moved

Regenerated by pnpm 10.31.0 only. ⛔ Not edited by hand.

- `pnpm update -r "@objectstack/*"` was tried first and REJECTED. It rewrote 30 manifests (every range raised to `^17.5.0`, and script keys reordered), and it re-resolved unrelated packages: `seroval`, `seroval-plugins`, `bson`, `@mongodb-js/saslprep`, `@microsoft/tsdoc-config`, `is-core-module`, `fast-uri`, `brace-expansion`, `use-sync-external-store`, and a second `dompurify`. None of those is `@objectstack`-caused.
- The route used instead: raise each `@objectstack/*` specifier to `^17.5.0` for ONE `pnpm install`; restore every manifest byte-for-byte to HEAD; run a second `pnpm install`, which reconciles the importers back to their declared ranges. The same raise-and-restore was then applied to the five direct `zod` specifiers (see below).
- Resolution census against the base lock (package@version keys, both directions):
  - removed: the seven `@objectstack/*` at 17.4.0;
  - added: the seven `@objectstack/*` at 17.5.0, and `zod@4.6.5`;
  - nothing else. No importer `specifier` line changes.
- Peer-suffix re-keys that follow from `zod@4.6.5` (same versions, new snapshot keys): `ai@7.0.65`, `@ai-sdk/gateway`, `@ai-sdk/mcp`, `@ai-sdk/provider-utils`, `@ai-sdk/react`, and the `fumadocs-core` / `fumadocs-mdx` / `fumadocs-ui` snapshots of `apps/site`.
- `zod@4.4.3` stays in the lock ONLY as `fumadocs-mdx`'s own dependency, unchanged from base. `@object-ui/site` type-checks green with it.

### Why `zod` moves (forced by the published 17.5.0 contract, not drift)

`@objectstack/spec@17.5.0` and `@objectstack/core@17.5.0` raise their `zod` range from `^4.4.3` to `^4.6.1`. With only the `@objectstack/*` entries moved, the lock resolved spec's `zod` to 4.6.5 while objectui's own direct `zod ^4.4.3` importers (`types`, `app-shell`, `components`, `plugin-timeline`, `test-support`) stayed on 4.4.3. Zod stamps its minor version into its types, so the two copies do not type-check against each other:

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build` failed with TS2345 in `src/zod/views.zod.ts`, bottoming out at "The types of '_zod.version.minor' are incompatible between these types. Type '4' is not assignable to type '6'."
- After the lock resolves objectui's `zod ^4.4.3` to the same 4.6.5 (a range it already admits; no manifest edit), the same build exits 0.

## Gates read on this head (`b732e17`)

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` | exit 0, "Lockfile is up to date" |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build` | exit 0 (was TS2345 before the `zod` resolution) |
| `turbo run build --filter=!@object-ui/site --concurrency=2` | 43/43 tasks successful |
| `turbo run type-check --concurrency=2` (unfiltered, 45 packages incl. `@object-ui/site`) | 81/81 tasks successful |
| `vitest run packages/types/` | RED: 56 failed in 15 files, 6376 passed |
| control: the same on the base tree (17.4.0 installed, detached worktree at `c80236e`) | 6432/6432 passed, 279/279 files |

So every one of the 56 reds is caused by the bump. The full suite is being read in four shards; its result is in the report comment.

## H3 / H4 — what the bump moves, by cause

The reds fall into three causes. Each row names the upstream change that forced it.

### Cause A — zod 4.4 to 4.6 internals (forced by the spec's `zod ^4.6.1`)

1. **A `.default()` member now reports `_zod.optin === 'defaulted'`**, a rung zod 4.4.3 did not have (it answered `'optional'`). `imported-defaults-8317.test.ts` ("no member became REQUIRED", 26 rows) compares the rung by equality, and the 9034 census counts a default-under-default as already optional. The production walker is NOT affected: `walk()` turns an inner `'defaulted'` into `'optional'` before `isAlreadyOptional` reads it, and the probe row "answers every probe exactly as the spec does" stays green for every imported schema. Adaptation: test-only, re-expressing "omissible" as either rung.
2. **zod's own strict-object `unrecognized_keys` is now `continue: true` (non-aborting).** In a union where the other arm aborts, the non-aborted arm is returned ALONE (`handleUnionResults`, whose code is unchanged).
   - `GridSchema.columns` (8516): the out-of-vocabulary key is now reported directly, as `unrecognized_keys` naming `xxl` at `columns`, instead of inside an `invalid_union`. The test's intent (the key is named) holds, and the author's message is better. Mechanical re-pin.
   - ⚠️ The dashboard widget slot (objectui#9256 in `content-channel-public-blocks-9256.test.ts`; `strict-widget-slot-registered-inputs-11022.test.ts`): `{ type: 'metric-card', value: 42, body: [] }` now yields ONE `unrecognized_keys` naming `value` and `body`. The by-name refusal ("`metric-card` reads NEITHER content channel") is GONE, and `value`, a registered input, is misreported as unrecognized. Base yields `invalid_union` carrying both arms. This is a regression in what an author (or an AI) is told, and restoring it is a design choice → left red, taken to the seat as a decision.

### Cause B — spec 17.5.0 makes an unknown-key refusal terminal

17.5.0's closed objects mark every `unrecognized_keys` issue `continue: false` (`markUnknownKeyRefusalTerminal` in the spec's dist). zod skips even a `when`-guarded check once the payload is explicitly aborted, so the two `superRefine` pointers (each carrying a `when` that always answers true) on `ObjectViewSchema` no longer run: `checkNamedViewCalendarAliases` (objectui#8355) and `checkNamedViewKanbanStrayGroupBy` (objectui#10321).

- The document is still REFUSED (by the spec, at `listViews.KEY.calendar` / `.kanban`).
- The spec's own message now guides `dateField` correctly ("does not say which end of the range it binds … Write the one you mean").
- For `endField` and `kanban.groupBy` it is a generic unrecognized-key message, so objectui's specific pointer is lost on the named-view route.
- Keep, rebuild or retire the pointer is a decision → left red.

### Cause C — the published contract moved, read by reference (the accept sets the seat's review reads)

| objectui surface (mirror by reference) | 17.4.0 | 17.5.0 | direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DetailViewFieldSchema.options[].visibleWhen` (spec `SelectOptionSchema`) | a whitespace-only string and a source-less `{ dialect, ast }` envelope accepted | both refused | narrower |
| `element:number` `dataSource.filter` (spec `ElementDataSourceSchema`) | the MongoDB-style record form (incl. `$and`/`$or`) and a CEL envelope accepted | only the `ViewFilterRule` array `[{ field, operator, value }]` | shape change, narrower for the record form |
| nested `calendar` block (spec `CalendarConfigSchema`) | `allDayField` refused by name | `allDayField` accepted | wider |
| `record:highlights` props (spec `RecordHighlightsProps`) | `aria`, `fields`, `layout` | adds `requiredPermissions`, `redactFields`, `enforceFieldSecurity` | wider |
| named view `listViews.KEY` (spec `ViewSchema`) | `pageName`, `tabs` live | both refused by name as retirement tombstones | narrower |
| spec `ListViewSchema` object-level checks | `checkListViewPageMount` present | gone | no objectui accept-set change (objectui never attached it) |
| spec `DashboardWidgetSchema` object-level checks | none | `checkDashboardWidgetStageOrder`, `checkDashboardWidgetMetricMeasureArity` | objectui's `.shape` mirror does not carry them, so objectui's door is now WIDER than the spec on both rules |
| spec `JoinedReportBlockSchema` | erased (`unknown`) | typed (`z.ZodObject`) | the objectui#10916 tripwire fires; the divergence pins compile green on 17.5.0 |

### H4 — consumer breaks

- Workspace build and type-check: no break (43/43, 81/81).
- Runtime (a test, not a type-check): ⚠️ the flow designer's fresh `wait` node. `defaultNodeExtras('wait')` seeds `{ waitEventConfig: { eventType: 'timer' } }`. Spec 17.5.0's `FlowNodeSchema` refuses a timer wait with no `timerDuration` (its message: a timer wait with no duration "parks the run forever while reporting success"). So a node the designer just created is refused at save. Failing check: `flow-canvas-seeds.spec-parse.test.tsx`, row "`wait`: a freshly added node parses as a spec FlowNode" (base: parses). Which default to seed is a product decision → left red.

## What the follow-up commits on this branch do, and what they leave red

Mechanical, each forced by a named upstream change (Cause A1, A2 for `GridSchema.columns`, and the Cause C re-pins that follow the spec by reference or follow a tripwire's own written instruction):

- the `optin` rung re-expression (8317, 9034);
- the `GridSchema.columns` issue-shape re-pin (8516);
- the objectui#10296 tripwires, done as their docblocks instruct at the pin bump: flip both rows to refusals, and delete the gated WIDER rows, their `WIDER_ARMS` entries and the `SpecEnvelopeAdmitsSourceless` gate;
- the `element:number` `dataSource.filter` rows re-pinned to the spec's verdicts, and `REBUILT_CLEAN` emptied (the spec's schema no longer reaches a `z.lazy`);
- the `record:highlights` PREMISE member list;
- the calendar spec-type fence (the doc fence tracks the SPEC type, so it gains `allDayField`) and the nested key list;
- the 7715 ListView row losing `checkListViewPageMount`, as its own message instructs.

Left RED on purpose, each with options in the report (`needs_decision`):

- Cause A2 widget-slot message regression (9256, 11022);
- Cause B named-view pointers (8355, 10321);
- `pageName` / `tabs` still declared on objectui's TypeScript named-view face while the protocol now retires them (7779; the objectui#8980 ruling kept them "declared inert" under a protocol that still declared them);
- the flow `wait` seed (H4);
- two sites that are consuming-card scope:
  - the 7715 DashboardWidget census row is objectui#9111's criterion;
  - the objectui#10916 tripwire is objectui#10940's burn-down, whose card says it "should land WITH that bump" — a published-type change this claim's surface excludes.

## Floors

This PR raises no floor. No code in it imports a 17.5.0-only export. The `^17.5.0` floors are left to the consuming cards, each at the moment it first imports a 17.5.0-only export: objectui#11013, objectui#11021, objectui#10188, objectui#7759, objectui#7347, objectui#8649, objectui#9217, objectui#10107 and objectui#9830. Each is unblocked by this landing; none is concluded by it.

## Acceptance notes

- **Consumer `zod` skew.** A consumer whose own lock holds `zod` 4.4.x and resolves `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 through objectui's `^17.x` ranges gets the same two-copy split measured above. That state already exists for any consumer today; it is not created here. Whether objectui's `zod` floor should rise to `^4.6.1` beside the consuming cards' spec floors is an open question in the report, not an edit here.
- **The 11-card addendum's objectui#9111 reading.** The addendum on objectui#11073 reads "Not met: objectui#9111 (`checkDashboardWidgetStageOrder` is still not exported on 17.5.0)". Measured here: it IS exported on 17.5.0 from `@objectstack/spec/ui`, and not from the root entry. The 7715 census sees it through `/ui`.
- The probes behind these readings were untracked scratch files, deleted before any commit; none is part of the diff.
